01

What it is

Model
Gibson Custom Shop Les Paul Custom Figured — "Dark Blue Widow Burst"
Year
2024 (decoded from serial)
Serial
CS 403228  = CS (Custom Shop) + 4 (2024) + 03228 (build no.)
Build type
Made-2-Measure / dealer-exclusive limited run — not a catalog production model
Family
"Widow" series — defined by colour-matched binding & coloured split-diamond headstock inlay

The certificate, the "Gibson Custom" stamp on the back of the headstock, and the oval "Gibson Custom" plate on the rear of the body confirm this is a genuine Nashville Custom Shop instrument — a meaningfully higher tier than a regular Gibson USA Les Paul Custom. The serial decodes cleanly on the modern Custom Shop pattern (CS + year-digit + build number), placing the build in 2024.

The "Widow" tag is the key to the finish. What separates a Blue Widow from an ordinary blue Les Paul Custom is the colour-matched treatment: the blue-tinted split-diamond headstock inlay, blue binding wrapping the body, neck and headstock, and the trans-blue burst over a hand-picked figured maple cap. Gibson has run the Widow theme in blue, red, purple, orange and green over the years — all low-volume Custom Shop pieces sold through select dealers, which is why you rarely see them on a big-box wall.

What the market says

Read "listed" (the asking price) and "sold" (what actually changed hands) as two different numbers. For this model the gap is small right now — these hold value unusually well for a modern Gibson because the runs are small and the colour has a cult following.

eBaySold~$6,750Closest clean comp is a 2024 Custom Shop (different model). Blue Widow eBay comps are thin; eBay runs softer than Reverb on high-end Gibsons due to ~13% fees.
Boutique dealersListed$6,500–7,500Eddie's, Wildwood, Cream City & similar — where these primarily trade.

The catch: those are dealer / retail numbers. A private seller does not net retail. After Reverb fees (~5%), shipping, and buyers expecting a discount versus a store with a warranty, a private national sale realistically nets somewhere around $5,200–$6,200. Selling locally only, in cash, lands lower again — and that's where the Denver-specific math comes in below.

The widest buyer pool and the only place the colour reliably finds its person. The $7,199 sold comp shows national demand is real. Price it well and it moves in weeks to ~2 months; the trade-off is packing, shipping a heavy guitar, and fee/return exposure.

Bottom line

If speed matters, a Denver shop hands you ~$4,000–$4,800 today (more in trade). If you want the most money and can wait, list it nationally on Reverb and net ~$5,500–$6,000. A local-only cash sale splits the difference on price but can sit for months because of the colour and the price point.

06

Helps & hurts

+ Adds value

  • Genuine Nashville Custom Shop — a full tier above Gibson USA; roughly double the resale of a USA Custom.
  • Rare Widow finish with the show-stopping colour-matched binding & headstock inlay — collectible and instantly recognisable.
  • Strong AAA figured top — the flame is dramatic; figure grade directly moves price.
  • Gold hardware & full Custom appointments (ebony board, pearl blocks, multi-ply binding).
  • Complete & correct — OHSC, COA, hang tags, paperwork. Completeness alone is worth several hundred dollars.
  • Near-mint & recent (2024) — modern Custom Shop QC is well regarded.

– Caps value

  • Polarising colour — blue Les Pauls have a far narrower buyer pool than a 'burst or black. It takes the right buyer, not any buyer.
  • Likely heavy — comparable Widows hit 9.7–10 lb. A 10+ lb weight turns some buyers off; weigh it and disclose.
  • 490R/498T pickups are standard Gibson units, not the Historic-grade Custombuckers purists prize.
  • Modern, not vintage/Historic — these depreciate like normal used gear once sold; they don't appreciate like a '59 reissue.
  • Not individually numbered — "rare" but not a numbered limited edition; several are on the market now, which tempers price.
  • Selling friction — fees (Reverb ~5%, eBay ~13%), shipping a heavy guitar, and any buckle rash / fret wear / finish checking would each chip away.
07

If you're unsure — how to verify

Run these checks before you list or sell. Each one either confirms the model or changes the number.

Custom Shop vs USA. Back of headstock should read "Gibson Custom" and there must be a COA. A plain "Gibson"-only headstock with no certificate is a USA model worth far less.
Decode the serial. Back of headstock. CS + year-digit + number = Custom Shop. Confirms the build year (here, 2024).
Confirm it's a Widow. Colour-matched binding and a coloured split-diamond inlay = Widow. White/cream binding with a plain pearl inlay = the standard trans-blue variant (often a touch less money).
Hardware colour. Gold is the premium Widow spec. Nickel "hand-selected top" versions also exist and can price slightly differently.
Identify the pickups. Pop a pickup ring or check the cavity. 490R/498T = standard. Custombuckers add desirability; EMG actives narrow the buyer pool. This genuinely moves price.
Weigh it. Put the number in any listing. Under ~9.5 lb helps; 10 lb+ hurts and should be disclosed up front.
Grade the top. Stronger, more 3-D flame = more money. Photograph it in raking light to show the figure.
Inspect the headstock & neck. The Achilles heel of Gibsons. Any headstock crack or repair is a major value hit — check the rear (Plate 05) under good light.

Methodology

Identification from submitted photographs and the Gibson Custom Certificate of Authenticity. Valuation triangulated from current dealer retail, completed Reverb sales, eBay completed listings, and active boutique-dealer asking prices for this model and its closest siblings, as of the issue date. Channel estimates apply standard resale spreads (dealers ~50–65% of resale; private national net after ~5% platform fees and shipping).

This is an informal market estimate for the owner's planning purposes — not a certified or insurance appraisal. Guitar values move with condition, weight, configuration, and demand; confirm the flagged items (pickups, weight, headstock condition) before relying on any figure. Visual styling is loosely inspired by Coal Creek Guitars (Englewood, CO); this document is independent and not affiliated with or issued by any retailer.
